The story behind it:
Every Sunday after church the whole house smelled like this. Nobody was allowed to lift the lid.

We still make it every Christmas Eve.
Ingredients (one per line):
3-4 lb chuck roast
2 tbsp oil
1 onion, quartered
4 carrots, cut in chunks
6 small potatoes
2 cups beef broth
1 packet onion soup mix
Salt and pepper
Instructions (one step per line):
1. Heat oven to 300°F.
2. Salt and pepper the roast, then brown it on all sides in oil in a Dutch oven.
3. Add the onion, broth and soup mix.
4. Cover and roast 2 hours.
5. Add carrots and potatoes, cover again and roast 1 more hour until fork-tender.
Notes & tips: Don't lift the lid! Leftovers make great sandwiches.

The story behind it: Made for every family reunion breakfast since the 70s.
Ingredients (one per line):
For the cake:
2 cups flour
1 cup sugar
2 tsp baking powder
1/2 tsp salt
1 cup milk
1 egg
1/3 cup melted butter
For the swirl:
1/2 cup brown sugar
2 tsp cinnamon
2 tbsp butter, softened
Instructions (one step per line):
Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a 9x9 pan.
Whisk the dry cake ingredients together.
Stir in milk, egg and melted butter until just combined.
Mix the swirl ingredients into a crumbly paste.
Pour half the batter in the pan, sprinkle half the swirl, repeat.
Bake 30-35 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.

The story behind it: Grandpa's one and only recipe, and he was very proud of it.
Ingredients (one per line):
1 graham cracker crust
1 can (14 oz) sweetened condensed milk
3 egg yolks
1/2 cup fresh lemon juice
Whipped cream for topping
Instructions (one step per line):
Whisk condensed milk and yolks.
Whisk in lemon juice until it thickens.
Pour into crust and bake 15 minutes at 350°F.
Cool, then chill at least 4 hours.
Top with whipped cream.

Ingredients (one per line):
4 ripe tomatoes
1/2 red onion, thinly sliced
2 tbsp olive oil
1 tbsp red wine vinegar
Fresh basil
Salt and pepper
Instructions (one step per line):
Slice tomatoes and onion.
Toss with oil, vinegar, salt and pepper.
Let sit 15 minutes, then tear basil over the top.
Notes & tips: Only make it when tomatoes are in season!
